steps.name: Test each ready pull request on main and the train before it
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
git config user.name "merge train"
git config user.email "merge-train@train.invalid"
main=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
echo "main=$main" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
image=$(sed -n 's/.*"sdk_image":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' prismpm.lock)
[[ $image =~ ^[a-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]{1,5})?/[a-z0-9./_-]+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]
scratch=$(mktemp -d)
export scratch image
trap 'rm -rf "$scratch"' EXIT
fast_gates() {
  node bootstrap/brand-sync.mjs --check &&
    python3 -I bootstrap/brand-fonts.py --check &&
    node bootstrap/frame-sync.mjs --check &&
    python3 -I tools/realize/gate.py --check &&
    python3 -I tools/standards/gate.py --check --base "$main" &&
    python3 -I tools/guests/gen.py check &&
    sh tools/generators/run.sh --check &&
    python3 -I tools/handwritten/gate.py --check --base "$main" &&
    docker run --rm \
      --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
      --volume "$scratch:/tmp" \
      --volume "$PWD:$PWD" \
      --workdir "$PWD" \
      --env HOME=/tmp/prismpm-home \
      --env PRISMPM_EPHEMERAL_HOME=1 \
      --env SDK_IMAGE="$image" \
      "$image" bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; mkdir -p "$HOME"; just fmt-check model template-check lint test'
}
# The browser acceptances on the merged tree, as the page job runs them on a
# pull request alone (CO-01 and the timing budgets failed on main after #145 and
# #161 were each green): a holo built from this tree, without the proof that
# main's own run binds, the page assembled around it, then every runner and
# every suite once. In a worktree of its own (the gates' own tests need git), so the train's tree stays what it merges, and in a
# shell of its own, because bash ignores errexit inside an if.
acceptances() {
  local copy=$RUNNER_TEMP/accept
  git worktree remove --force "$copy" 2>/dev/null || rm -rf "$copy"
  git worktree add -q --detach "$copy" HEAD
  mkdir -p "$scratch/prismpm-home/.docker"
  printf '{}\n' >"$scratch/prismpm-home/.docker/config.json"
  (
    cd "$copy"
    shopt -s nullglob globstar
    docker run --rm \
      --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
      --group-add "$(stat -c '%g' /var/run/docker.sock)" \
      --volume "$scratch:/tmp" \
      --volume "$PWD:$PWD" \
      --volume /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
      --workdir "$PWD" \
      --env DOCKER_CONFIG=/tmp/prismpm-home/.docker \
      --env BUILDX_CONFIG=/tmp/prismpm-buildx \
      --env HOME=/tmp/prismpm-home \
      --env PRISMPM_EPHEMERAL_HOME=1 \
      --env SDK_IMAGE="$image" \
      "$image" bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; prismpm --project app build --no-provenance'
    holos=(app/.prism/build/*/*.holo)
    [[ ${#holos[@]} -eq 1 ]]
    fingerprint=$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8")).archive_fingerprint)' "$(dirname "${holos[0]}")/application/holo-identities.json")
    "$RUNNER_TEMP/draw/bin/python" -I bootstrap/og.py
    "$RUNNER_TEMP/draw/bin/python" -I bootstrap/icons.py
    cp "${holos[0]}" site/app.holo
    cp -r try/vendor site/vendor
    rm -rf site/vendor/prism-code/fixtures site/vault/test
    node -e '
      const { readFileSync, writeFileSync } = require("node:fs");
      const [id, url] = process.argv.slice(1);
      const app = JSON.parse(readFileSync("site/app.json", "utf8"));
      app.attestations ??= {};
      app.attestations.build = { id, url };
      writeFileSync("site/app.json", `${JSON.stringify(app, null, 2)}\n`);
    ' "$fingerprint" "$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID"
    node bootstrap/page.mjs site
    for objects in bootstrap/*-objects.mjs; do node "$objects" site; done
    node bootstrap/precache.mjs site
    export NODE_PATH="$(npm root --global)"
    runners=(test/*/run.mjs)
    suites=(test/**/*.test.mjs)
    for runner in "${runners[@]}"; do node "$runner"; done
    # The gates of the product record's time behaviour measures, one at a time and apart from the rest (as the page check runs them).
    mapfile -t timed < <(node --input-type=module -e 'import { load } from "./tools/specs/record.mjs"; console.log([...new Set(load("app/specs/product/spec.json").quality.filter((q) => q.subcharacteristic === "time behaviour").flatMap((q) => q.measures.map((m) => m.gate)))].join("\n"))')
    rest=()
    for suite in "${suites[@]}"; do [[ " ${timed[*]} " == *" $suite "* ]] || rest+=("$suite"); done
    node --test --test-concurrency=1 "${timed[@]}"
    node --test "${rest[@]}"
  )
}
ready=()
: >"$RUNNER_TEMP/refused"
while read -r number head draft fork; do
  [[ $draft == false && $fork == false ]] || continue
  ok=true
  for name in "page / gates" "acceptance / ubuntu-24.04"; do
    state=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/$head/check-runs" -f check_name="$name" -X GET --jq '[.check_runs[] | .conclusion][0] // "pending"')
    [[ $state == success ]] || ok=false
    # A check that ended without passing is said once, so a pull request is never left waiting in silence.
    more=
    [[ $state != cancelled ]] || more=" (a check cancelled at its time limit kept no proof; a new run finds main's kept proof only once main's own acceptance run for its commit has finished)"
    case $state in success | pending) ;; *) printf '%s %s %s\n' "$number" "$head" "its check \"$name\" ended $state on this head, so it is not green; push to this branch to run it again$more" >>"$RUNNER_TEMP/refused" ;; esac
  done
  if $ok; then ready+=("$number:$head"); fi
done < <(gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls?state=open&base=main&sort=created&direction=asc&per_page=50" \
  --jq '.[] | "\(.number) \(.head.sha) \(.draft) \(.head.repo.full_name != .base.repo.full_name)"')
# A pull request that names an open deploy-blocked issue in its description is
# there to get the live page moving again, so it boards first: pull requests
# ahead of it by number cannot then make the gates refuse it round after round
# (#181 was refused twice that way while main's deploy stayed blocked).
blocking=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues?state=open&labels=deploy-blocked&per_page=20" --jq '[.[].number | tostring] | join("|")')
first=()
later=()
for entry in "${ready[@]}"; do
  if [[ -n $blocking ]] && gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls/${entry%%:*}" --jq '.body // ""' | grep -qE "#($blocking)([^0-9]|$)"; then first+=("$entry"); else later+=("$entry"); fi
done
ready=("${first[@]}" "${later[@]}")
echo "ready: ${ready[*]:-none}"
# What the acceptances need on the runner, installed once and before any pull request's code runs.
if [[ ${#ready[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
  npm install --no-audit --no-fund --global playwright@1.56.1
  playwright install --with-deps chromium
  python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/draw"
  "$RUNNER_TEMP/draw/bin/pip" install --quiet --no-deps --only-binary :all: --require-hashes -r bootstrap/draw-requirements.txt
fi
# The fast gates and the browser acceptances take about forty minutes, so the
# train runs them once, on the tree of all the pull requests that merge onto
# main together, and one by one only when that tree fails, to find which of
# them it refuses. What is tested is still exactly the tree that merges.
gates() { # gates LOG: the fast gates and the browser acceptances on HEAD; the pull requests' own code runs without the token
  (unset GH_TOKEN; fast_gates && bash -euo pipefail -c "$(declare -f acceptances); acceptances") >"$1" 2>&1
}
said() { # said LOG: what refused, in the log's own words, on one line
  tail -n 40 "$1" >&2
  # A gate that passes says so in the same form as one that refuses, and the gates stop at the first refusal: the last lines are the ones that refused.
  grep -E '^ *not ok |^gate failed|^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]-[0-9]+: ' "$1" | grep -v ' is what ' | sed 's/^ *//' | tr -d '@`' | tail -n 4 | paste -sd ';' | cut -c1-900
}
# Two pull requests that each add a part or a module both change files the model
# writes from others: the entry points of app/lexlean.toml, its lock, and the
# committed outputs of the generators' steps. Git cannot merge those, so each was
# refused round after round while another landed (#223, twice). They are not a
# pull request's own words, so the train writes them again on the merged tree,
# whenever both sides changed one. The gates then run on exactly that tree.
regenerated() { # regenerated COMMIT: the files the model writes from others, as COMMIT's steps name them
  printf '%s\n' app/lexlean.toml app/lexlean.lock
  git grep -h -o '"output": *"[^"]*"' "$1" -- 'generators/*/steps.json' 'generators/*/steps/*.json' | cut -d'"' -f4 | grep -v -e '^\.gen/' -e '^\.github/' | sort -u
}
regenerate() { # regenerate: on the merge in progress, the entry points of both sides, every generator's outputs and the lock
  local f
  if [[ -n $(git ls-files -u app/lexlean.toml) ]]; then
    node -e '
      const { execFileSync } = require("node:child_process");
      const [base, ours, theirs] = [1, 2, 3].map((n) => execFileSync("git", ["show", `:${n}:app/lexlean.toml`], { encoding: "utf8" }).split("\n"));
      const at = (lines) => lines.findIndex((l) => /^entrypoints = \[.*\]$/.test(l));
      const [b, o, t] = [base, ours, theirs].map((lines) => new Set([...lines[at(lines)].matchAll(/"([^"]+)"/g)].map((m) => m[1])));
      const rest = (lines) => lines.filter((_, i) => i !== at(lines)).join("\n");
      // Only the entry points may differ three ways; an entry point either side took away stays away.
      const keep = rest(theirs) === rest(base) ? ours : rest(ours) === rest(base) || rest(ours) === rest(theirs) ? theirs : process.exit(1);
      const entries = [...new Set([...o, ...t])].filter((e) => !b.has(e) || (o.has(e) && t.has(e))).sort();
      keep[at(keep)] = `entrypoints = [${entries.map((e) => `"${e}"`).join(", ")}]`;
      require("node:fs").writeFileSync("app/lexlean.toml", keep.join("\n"));
    '
    git add app/lexlean.toml
  fi
  for f in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U); do git checkout -q --ours -- "$f"; done
  sh tools/generators/run.sh
  docker run --rm \
    --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
    --volume "$scratch:/tmp" \
    --volume "$PWD:$PWD" \
    --workdir "$PWD/app" \
    --env HOME=/tmp/prismpm-home \
    --env PRISMPM_EPHEMERAL_HOME=1 \
    --env SDK_IMAGE="$image" \
    "$image" bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; mkdir -p "$HOME"; lexlean lock'
  git add -A
}
board() { # board together|each: merge each of the queue onto HEAD (each: where it passes the gates there)
  local entry number head before base both outside
  boarded=()
  for entry in "${queue[@]}"; do
    number=${entry%%:*}
    head=${entry#*:}
    before=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
    git fetch -q origin "$head"
    base=$(git merge-base HEAD "$head")
    regenerated HEAD >"$RUNNER_TEMP/regenerated"
    both=$(comm -12 <(git diff --name-only "$base" HEAD | sort) <(git diff --name-only "$base" "$head" | sort) | grep -xFf "$RUNNER_TEMP/regenerated" | paste -sd ' ' || true)
    git merge -q --no-ff --no-commit "$head" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    outside=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U | grep -vxFf "$RUNNER_TEMP/regenerated" | paste -sd ' ' || true)
    if [[ -n $outside ]]; then
      git merge --abort || true
      printf '%s %s %s\n' "$number" "$head" "it conflicts with main ($main) and the pull requests the train takes before it, in $outside" >>"$RUNNER_TEMP/refused"
      continue
    fi
    # The pull request's code runs here, so without the token, and in a shell of its own, because bash ignores errexit inside an if.
    if [[ -n $both ]] && ! (unset GH_TOKEN; bash -euo pipefail -c "$(declare -f regenerate); regenerate") >"$RUNNER_TEMP/regenerate-$number.log" 2>&1; then
      tail -n 20 "$RUNNER_TEMP/regenerate-$number.log" >&2
      git reset -q --hard "$before"
      git clean -fdq
      printf '%s %s %s\n' "$number" "$head" "it and the train before it both change files the model writes from others ($both), and writing them again on the merged tree failed; see run $GITHUB_RUN_ID" >>"$RUNNER_TEMP/refused"
      continue
    fi
    [[ ! -e .git/MERGE_HEAD ]] || git commit -q -m "Merge pull request #$number (merge train)"
    [[ -z $both ]] || echo "#$number $head: written again on the merged tree, because both sides changed $both"
    if [[ $1 == together ]] || gates "$RUNNER_TEMP/gates-$number.log"; then
      boarded+=("$entry")
      echo "#$number $head: boards on main and the train before it ($1)"
    else
      printf '%s %s %s\n' "$number" "$head" "the fast gates or the browser acceptances refuse it merged with main ($main) and the pull requests the train takes before it; see run $GITHUB_RUN_ID. They say: $(said "$RUNNER_TEMP/gates-$number.log")" >>"$RUNNER_TEMP/refused"
      git reset -q --hard "$before"
    fi
  done
}
queue=("${ready[@]}")
board together
if [[ ${#boarded[@]} -gt 0 ]] && ! gates "$RUNNER_TEMP/gates-train.log"; then
  why=$(said "$RUNNER_TEMP/gates-train.log")
  echo "the gates refuse ${boarded[*]} together ($why)"
  git reset -q --hard "$main"
  if [[ ${#boarded[@]} -eq 1 ]]; then
    printf '%s %s %s\n' "${boarded[0]%%:*}" "${boarded[0]#*:}" "the fast gates or the browser acceptances refuse it merged with main ($main); see run $GITHUB_RUN_ID. They say: $why" >>"$RUNNER_TEMP/refused"
    boarded=()
  else
    queue=("${boarded[@]}")
    board each
  fi
fi
accepted=("${boarded[@]}")
echo "accepted=${accepted[*]:-}" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
# What the train tested travels to the merge job as its commits: a tree with
# files written again is not one GitHub's own merge would make.
mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/train"
git branch -q -f train HEAD
[[ ${#accepted[@]} -eq 0 ]] || git bundle create -q "$RUNNER_TEMP/train/train.bundle" "$main..train"
# The refusals travel to the merge job as an output.
cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/refused"
echo "refused=$(base64 -w0 <"$RUNNER_TEMP/refused")" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

#: Ready: open, from this repository, not a draft, and both required
checks passed on its head. The fast gates are the ones that take
seconds to minutes: every gate the page job runs before the proof
(brand and frame locks, RZ-01, HW-01's ratchet and ST-01, the last two
against main), the parts, product and guest gates natively, then the
workspace's format, model, template, lint and test gates in the
locked SDK. The proof is not repeated: main's own run binds it.

steps.name: Hand the train's commits to the merge job
Switch GitHub's auto-merge off, merge the accepted in order, and say why the rest wait
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
query='mutation($pr: ID!) { disablePullRequestAutoMerge(input: {pullRequestId: $pr}) { clientMutationId } }'
gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls?state=open&base=main&per_page=50" --jq '.[] | select(.auto_merge != null) | .node_id' |
  while read -r id; do gh api graphql -f query="$query" -f pr="$id" >/dev/null || true; done
# Every open pull request learns once, from the pipeline, how it merges.
notice="Merge train notice"
gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls?state=open&base=main&per_page=50" --jq '.[].number' |
  while read -r number; do
    seen=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$number/comments?per_page=100" | jq --arg m "$notice" '[.[] | select(.body | startswith($m))] | length')
    if [[ $seen == 0 ]]; then
      gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/issues/$number/comments" -f body="$(printf '%s\n' "$notice: the merge train merges this pull request once it is green on current main; don't enable auto-merge." '' '---' '_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_')" >/dev/null || true
    fi
  done
# The train's commits, checked without running anything of theirs: each is the
# train before it merged with the accepted head, and differs from what git
# itself merges only in files the model writes from others. Where none differs,
# GitHub merges as ever. Where one does, the train pushes the commits it tested.
regenerated() { # regenerated COMMIT: the files the model writes from others, as COMMIT's steps name them
  printf '%s\n' app/lexlean.toml app/lexlean.lock
  git grep -h -o '"output": *"[^"]*"' "$1" -- 'generators/*/steps.json' 'generators/*/steps/*.json' | cut -d'"' -f4 | grep -v -e '^\.gen/' -e '^\.github/' | sort -u
}
entries=($ACCEPTED)
failed=0
odd=-1
if [[ ${#entries[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
  git fetch -q "$RUNNER_TEMP/train/train.bundle" train
  tip=$(git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD)
  mapfile -t chain < <(git rev-list --first-parent --reverse "$MAIN..$tip")
  sound=true
  [[ ${#chain[@]} -eq ${#entries[@]} ]] || sound=false
  prev=$MAIN
  for i in "${!entries[@]}"; do
    $sound || break
    c=${chain[i]}
    if [[ $(git rev-parse "$c^1") != "$prev" || $(git rev-parse "$c^2") != "${entries[i]#*:}" || -n $(git rev-parse -q --verify "$c^3" || true) ]]; then sound=false; break; fi
    tree=$(git merge-tree --write-tree "$prev" "${entries[i]#*:}" | head -n 1) || true
    changed=$(git diff --name-only "$tree" "$c^{tree}")
    if [[ -n $changed ]]; then
      [[ $odd -ge 0 ]] || odd=$i
      [[ -z $(grep -vxFf <(regenerated "$prev") <<<"$changed" || true) ]] || sound=false
    fi
    prev=$c
  done
  if ! $sound; then
    echo "::error::the train's commits are not main and the accepted pull requests merged in order with only regenerated files written again; nothing merges"
    entries=()
    failed=1
  elif [[ $odd -ge 0 ]]; then
    now=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/main" --jq .sha)
    if [[ $now != "$MAIN" ]]; then
      echo "::notice::main moved to $now outside the train; the next run tests ${entries[*]} again"
      entries=()
    elif git push -q "https://x-access-token:$GH_TOKEN@github.com/$REPO" "$tip:refs/heads/main"; then
      echo "pushed the train as tested: main is $tip, with ${entries[*]}"
      entries=()
    else
      printf '%s %s %s\n' "${entries[odd]%%:*}" "${entries[odd]#*:}" "it and the train before it both change files the model writes from others, and GitHub refused the push of the tree the train tested with them written again (see run $RUN)" >>refused-merge.txt
      entries=("${entries[@]:0:odd}")
    fi
  fi
fi
expected=$MAIN
for entry in "${entries[@]}"; do
  number=${entry%%:*}
  head=${entry#*:}
  now=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/main" --jq .sha)
  if [[ $now != "$expected" ]]; then
    echo "::notice::main moved to $now outside the train; the next run tests #$number again"
    break
  fi
  if ! expected=$(gh api -X PUT "repos/$REPO/pulls/$number/merge" -f sha="$head" -f merge_method=merge --jq .sha); then
    printf '%s %s %s\n' "$number" "$head" "GitHub refused the merge (see run $RUN)" >>refused-merge.txt
    break
  fi
  echo "merged #$number at $expected"
done
mkdir -p refused
printf '%s' "$REFUSED" | base64 -d >refused/refused.txt
cat refused-merge.txt >>refused/refused.txt 2>/dev/null || true
while read -r number head why; do
  [[ -n $number ]] || continue
  marker="Merge train: $head"
  seen=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$number/comments?per_page=100" | jq --arg m "$marker" '[.[] | select(.body | startswith($m))] | length')
  if [[ $seen == 0 ]]; then
    gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/issues/$number/comments" -f body="$(printf '%s\n' "$marker: not merged, because $why. Fix it on this branch (merge main first) and the train tests it again." '' '---' '_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_')" >/dev/null
  fi
done <refused/refused.txt
exit "$failed"

#: GitHub's own auto-merge would merge behind the train's back.

name: Two pull requests that each pass their gates against an older main can
still break main together: #105 and #110 were each green, and together
ST-01 refused main. So nothing merges on its own. The train merges a pull
request only after the fast gates passed on it merged with main as main is
now, together with every pull request the train takes before it.
One run at a time. The test job has a read-only token and runs each ready
pull request's code. The merge job never runs that code: it merges the
accepted pull requests in order, and only while main is still where they
were tested.
Files the model writes from others (the entry points, the lock, the
generators' committed outputs) are written again on the merged tree when
both sides changed them, so two pull requests that each add a part do not
refuse each other. The merge job then pushes the commits the train tested.
